newsitem.title: USA: Lincoln National to buy CIGNA's life unit for $1.4 billion.
newsitem.headline: Lincoln National to buy CIGNA's life unit for $1.4 billion.

text.p: Lincoln National Corp. said on Monday it will buy CIGNA Corp.'s individual life insurance and annuity business for about $1.4 billion in cash.
Lincoln National said the deal, which is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to close by year-end, should add to its 1998 earnings immediately.
Fort Wayne, Ind.-based Lincoln National said it expects substantially increased sales from the combined businesses and expects to realise pretax expense savings of $40 million by 1999.

CIGNA, based in Philadelphia, said it expects to use the proceeds from the sale of the business to repurchase its shares. However, the company said it also may use the proceeds for internal growth or acquisitions.

"This transaction will bring together CIGNA's premier individual life insurance operations with Lincoln Life's leading annuity business to create one of the most powerful financial planning organisations in the country," Lincoln National Chief Executive Ian Rolland said in a statement.

Lincoln National in June agreed to sell its 83.3 percent stake in American States Financial Corp., a property-casualty business, as it increased its focus on its life insurance, annuities and mutual funds businesses.
The sale of that business is expected to produce proceeds of $2.15 billion after tax.

Lincoln National said the transaction, the largest in its history, will be accomplished through an indemnity reinsurance agreement. Lincoln National will receive the assets and liabilities of the acquired businesses. CIGNA will retain its statutory surplus from the businesses, which at the end of 1996 was about $225 million.
Operations will continue in both Fort Wayne and the Hartford, Conn., area, where CIGNA's Individual Insurance business has its headhquarters.

Lincoln National said the transaction will bring CIGNA Financial Advisors, a career agency system with 600 agents, a life brokerage operation, and an annuity distribution system, as well as about $37 billion of individual life insurance in force.
CIGNA's corporate-owned life insurance, group life insurance, and life, health and accident reinsurance businesses are not part of the transaction.
"We believe this is an attractive transaction for CIGNA and its shareholders," CIGNA Chief Executive Wilson Taylor said in a statement.
"The individual life insurance and annuity operation is a strong business with solid returns, but has limited strategic connection to our other businesses," he said.
"The sale of this business, combined with our recent acquisition of Healthsource, an HMO and health insurance company, will strengthen our financial and strategic position," he said.
